subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw apply to externally, plugin, or agent-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs before they can run on inherited provider/model defaults?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes cron activation defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model cost policy, quota thresholds, and upgrade behavior that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
options.body: Require operator-visible approval or explicit activation for non-operator recurring agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and define doctor/update migration behavior together.

options.title: Narrow model-cost guard first
options.body: Warn or block only when recurring jobs inherit expensive defaults while leaving activation and provenance to separate follow-up work.

options.title: Split into canonical sub-issues
options.body: Use #71712, #14376, and #42475 as the implementation owners for provenance, recurring guardrails, and budget enforcement while keeping this issue as the user-impact umbrella.

recommendation.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible approval or explicit activation for non-operator recurring agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and define doctor/update migration behavior together.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-boundary product/security policy choice, and steipete has the strongest available history on the affected cron model-selection and scheduling surface.
